pairs.verbatim: Brandon T. Willard and R´emi Louf. Efficient guided generation for large language models.ArXiv, abs/2307.09702, 2023.
pairs.why: Outlines demonstrates that behavior constraints can be enforced purely through standard decode-time logit processor interfaces (no internal hooks needed), the same deployability mechanism LogitGate relies on to make activation-steering-like control usable without mid-layer hooks.
pairs.oa_title: Efficient Guided Generation for Large Language Models

pairs.title: Programming refusal with conditional activation steering
pairs.authors: Bruce W. Lee, Inkit Padhi, K. Ramamurthy, Erik Miehling, Pierre L. Dognin, Manish Nagireddy, Amit Dhurandhar
pairs.verbatim: Bruce W. Lee, Inkit Padhi, K. Ramamurthy, Erik Miehling, Pierre L. Dognin, Manish Nagireddy, and Amit Dhurandhar. Programming refusal with conditional activation steering.ArXiv, abs/2409.05907, 2024.
pairs.why: CAST extends conditional/gated activation steering to another behavior (refusal) but still requires mid-layer hooks, illustrating the same hook-dependency limitation that LogitGate's purpose is to remove.
pairs.oa_title: Programming Refusal with Conditional Activation Steering

pairs.title: Forever: Forgetting curve-inspired memory replay for language model continual learning
pairs.authors: Yujie Feng, Hao Wang, Jian Li, Xu Chu, Zhaolu Kang, Yiran Liu, Yasha Wang, Philip S. Yu, Xiao-Ming Wu
pairs.verbatim: Yujie Feng, Hao Wang, Jian Li, Xu Chu, Zhaolu Kang, Yiran Liu, Yasha Wang, Philip S. Yu, and Xiao-Ming Wu. Forever: Forgetting curve-inspired memory replay for language model continual learning. 2026.
pairs.why: FOREVER is the exact parameter-space replay-scheduling baseline that KL-Time Replay directly replaces/extends with a function-space signal; the paper's whole framing is 'FOREVER but function-space'.
pairs.oa_title: FOREVER: Forgetting Curve-Inspired Memory Replay for Language Model Continual Learning

pairs.title: Learn the time to learn: Replay scheduling in continual learning
pairs.authors: Marcus Klasson, Hedvig Kjellstrom, Chen Zhang
pairs.verbatim: Marcus Klasson, Hedvig Kjellstrom, and Chen Zhang. Learn the time to learn: Replay scheduling in continual learning. Trans. Mach. Learn. Res., 2023, 2022.
pairs.why: Directly addresses the same 'when to replay' scheduling problem the paper targets, learning replay schedules rather than fixing them by step count.
pairs.oa_title: Learn the Time to Learn: Replay Scheduling in Continual Learning

pairs.title: Anchored supervised fine-tuning
pairs.authors: He Zhu, Junyou Su, Peng Lai, Ren Ma, Wenjia Zhang, Linyi Yang, Guanhua Chen
pairs.verbatim: He Zhu, Junyou Su, Peng Lai, Ren Ma, Wenjia Zhang, Linyi Yang, and Guanhua Chen. Anchored supervised fine-tuning. ArXiv, abs/2509.23753, 2025.
pairs.why: Uses forward-KL anchoring on fixed anchor points to monitor/stabilize function-space behavior during training, the same core mechanism (KL divergence on anchors) this paper repurposes for replay scheduling instead of regularization.
pairs.oa_title: Anchored Supervised Fine-Tuning

pairs.title: Quiet-STaR: Language models can teach themselves to think before speaking
pairs.authors: Eric Zelikman, Georges Harik, Yijia Shao, Varuna Jayasiri, Nick Haber, Noah D. Goodman
pairs.verbatim: Eric Zelikman, Georges Harik, Yijia Shao, Varuna Jayasiri, Nick Haber, and Noah D Goodman. Quiet-star: Language models can teach themselves to think before speaking. arXiv preprint arXiv:2403.09629, 2024.
pairs.why: Quiet-STaR already studies self-improving CoT reasoning directly on unstructured, general-purpose pretraining text (the 'far end' of the spectrum the intermediate benchmark is meant to bridge toward), so it is the closest existing work on the same underlying purpose.
pairs.oa_title: Quiet-STaR: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Think Before Speaking

pairs.title: Measuring massive multitask language understanding
pairs.authors: Dan Hendrycks, Collin Burns, Steven Basart, Andy Zou, Mantas Mazeika, Dawn Song, Jacob Steinhardt
pairs.verbatim: Dan Hendrycks, Collin Burns, Steven Basart, Andy Zou, Mantas Mazeika, Dawn Song, and Jacob Steinhardt. Measuring massive multitask language understanding. arXiv preprint arXiv:2009.03300, 2020.
pairs.why: MMLU is the curated QA dataset (the other 'end' of the spectrum) that the paper directly modifies to build its intermediate benchmark MMLU-FREE-FORM, so it defines the exact baseline the new resource is positioned as intermediate to.
pairs.oa_title: Measuring Massive Multitask Language Understanding

pairs.title: GPQA: A graduate-level Google-proof Q&A benchmark
pairs.authors: David Rein, Betty Li Hou, Asa Cooper Stickland, Jackson Petty, Richard Yuanzhe Pang, Julien Dirani, Julian Michael, Samuel R. Bowman
pairs.verbatim: David Rein, Betty Li Hou, Asa Cooper Stickland, Jackson Petty, Richard Yuanzhe Pang, Julien Dirani, Julian Michael, and Samuel R Bowman. Gpqa: A graduate-level google-proof q&a benchmark. arXiv preprint arXiv:2311.12022, 2023.
pairs.why: Cited by the paper as evidence that curating large-scale (question, CoT, answer) datasets is prohibitively expensive, which is exactly the motivation the paper uses to justify needing a cheaper intermediate benchmark.
pairs.oa_title: GPQA: A Graduate-Level Google-Proof Q&A Benchmark

pairs.title: Judging LLM-as-a-judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
pairs.authors: Lianmin Zheng, Wei-Lin Chiang, Ying Sheng, Siyuan Zhuang, Zhanghao Wu, Yonghao Zhuang, Zi Lin, Zhuohan Li, Dacheng Li, Eric Xing, Hao Zhang, Joseph E. Gonzalez, Ion Stoica
pairs.venue: Thirty-seventh Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems Datasets and Benchmarks Track
pairs.verbatim: Lianmin Zheng, Wei-Lin Chiang, Ying Sheng, Siyuan Zhuang, Zhanghao Wu, Yonghao Zhuang, Zi Lin, Zhuohan Li, Dacheng Li, Eric Xing, Hao Zhang, Joseph E. Gonzalez, and Ion Stoica. Judging LLM-as-a-judge with MT-bench and chatbot arena. In Thirty-seventh Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems Datasets and Benchmarks Track, 2023.
pairs.why: The paper explicitly draws its core mechanism from this work, adapting the LLM-as-a-judge framework (rating answers for quality rather than exact alignment) into speculative-decoding verification.
pairs.oa_title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena

pairs.title: Speculative decoding with big little decoder
pairs.authors: Sehoon Kim, Karttikeya Mangalam, Suhong Moon, Jitendra Malik, Michael W. Mahoney, Amir Gholami, Kurt Keutzer
pairs.venue: Thirty-seventh Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems
pairs.verbatim: Sehoon Kim, Karttikeya Mangalam, Suhong Moon, Jitendra Malik, Michael W. Mahoney, Amir Gholami, and Kurt Keutzer. Speculative decoding with big little decoder. In Thirty-seventh Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems, 2023.
pairs.why: Already proposes a verification/acceptance decision that goes beyond a strict draft/target probability-alignment ratio (using an uncertainty measure to decide when the target should intervene), directly overlapping the paper's stated purpose of moving verification beyond alignment.
pairs.oa_title: Speculative Decoding with Big Little Decoder

pairs.title: Online speculative decoding
pairs.authors: Xiaoxuan Liu, Lanxiang Hu, Peter Bailis, Ion Stoica, Zhijie Deng, Alvin Cheung, Hao Zhang
pairs.verbatim: Xiaoxuan Liu, Lanxiang Hu, Peter Bailis, Ion Stoica, Zhijie Deng, Alvin Cheung, and Hao Zhang. Online speculative decoding. arXiv preprint arXiv:2310.07177, 2023.
pairs.why: Cited by the paper directly at the point where it argues standard verification rejects tokens because it 'seeks alignment with its own response rather than contextual accuracy'; this work already targets that alignment gap (via online adaptation) rather than raw acceptance-probability matching.
pairs.oa_title: Online Speculative Decoding

pairs.title: FasterMoE: modeling and optimizing training of large-scale dynamic pre-trained models
pairs.authors: Jiaao He, Jidong Zhai, Tiago Antunes, Haojie Wang, Fuwen Luo, Shangfeng Shi, Qin Li
pairs.venue: PPoPP '22: 27th ACM SIGPLAN Symposium on Principles and Practice of Parallel Programming
pairs.verbatim: Jiaao He, Jidong Zhai, Tiago Antunes, Haojie Wang, Fuwen Luo, Shangfeng Shi, and Qin Li. Fastermoe: modeling and optimizing training of large-scale dynamic pre-trained models. In PPoPP '22: 27th ACM SIGPLAN Symposium on Principles and Practice of Parallel Programming, Seoul, Republic of Korea, April 2 - 6, 2022, pp. 120-134, 2022.
pairs.why: Targets exactly the same goal (reduce All-to-All communication cost in MoE training by exploiting expert-routing locality) but from the model/expert-placement perspective; the paper explicitly contrasts NetMoE's 'unexplored sample perspective' against this and other dynamic-expert-placement works.
pairs.oa_title: FasterMoE: modeling and optimizing training of large-scale dynamic pre-trained models

pairs.title: FlexMoE: Scaling large-scale sparse pre-trained model training via dynamic device placement
pairs.authors: Xiaonan Nie, Xupeng Miao, Zilong Wang, Zichao Yang, Jilong Xue, Lingxiao Ma, Gang Cao, Bin Cui
pairs.verbatim: Xiaonan Nie, Xupeng Miao, Zilong Wang, Zichao Yang, Jilong Xue, Lingxiao Ma, Gang Cao, and Bin Cui. Flexmoe: Scaling large-scale sparse pre-trained model training via dynamic device placement. Proc. ACM Manag. Data, 1(1):110:1-110:19, 2023.
pairs.why: Another direct prior-art instance of dynamically adjusting placement (of devices/experts, not samples) to reduce All-to-All communication cost based on routing locality, the same problem NetMoE addresses from the opposite (sample) side.
pairs.oa_title: FlexMoE: Scaling Large-scale Sparse Pre-trained Model Training via Dynamic Device Placement

pairs.title: BASE layers: Simplifying training of large, sparse models
pairs.authors: Mike Lewis, Shruti Bhosale, Tim Dettmers, Naman Goyal, Luke Zettlemoyer
pairs.venue: International Conference on Machine Learning, ICML 2021, volume 139, pp. 6265-6274
pairs.verbatim: Mike Lewis, Shruti Bhosale, Tim Dettmers, Naman Goyal, and Luke Zettlemoyer. BASE layers: Simplifying training of large, sparse models. In International Conference on Machine Learning, ICML 2021, 18-24 July 2021, Virtual Event, volume 139, pp. 6265-6274, 2021.
pairs.why: Represents the competing 'modify the model definition/routing' family of solutions to the same All-to-All bottleneck, which the paper cites as an alternative (but convergence-affecting) approach to the load-balancing problem it solves via sample placement instead.
pairs.oa_title: BASE Layers: Simplifying Training of Large, Sparse Models

pairs.title: GPT-4 technical report
pairs.authors: Josh Achiam, Steven Adler, Sandhini Agarwal, et al.
pairs.verbatim: Josh Achiam, Steven Adler, Sandhini Agarwal, Lama Ahmad, Ilge Akkaya, Florencia Leoni Aleman, Diogo Almeida, Janko Altenschmidt, Sam Altman, Shyamal Anadkat, et al. GPT-4 technical report. OpenAI, 2023.
pairs.why: States the 'contamination has very little effect' position that the paper's unifying, setting-dependent takeaway is designed to reconcile with the opposing view that contamination matters.
pairs.oa_title: GPT-4 Technical Report

pairs.title: Benchmark data contamination of large language models: A survey
pairs.authors: Cheng Xu, Shuhao Guan, Derek Greene, M. Kechadi, et al.
pairs.verbatim: Cheng Xu, Shuhao Guan, Derek Greene, M Kechadi, et al. Benchmark data contamination of large language models: A survey. arXiv preprint arXiv:2406.04244, 2024.
pairs.why: Explicitly challenges the GPT-4 report's 'little effect' conclusion, forming exactly the unresolved tension in the literature that the paper's setting-dependent claim is presented as reconciling.
pairs.oa_title: Benchmark Data Contamination of Large Language Models: A Survey

pairs.title: Investigating data contamination for pre-training language models
pairs.authors: Minhao Jiang, Ken Ziyu Liu, Ming Zhong, Rylan Schaeffer, Siru Ouyang, Jiawei Han, Sanmi Koyejo
pairs.verbatim: Minhao Jiang, Ken Ziyu Liu, Ming Zhong, Rylan Schaeffer, Siru Ouyang, Jiawei Han, and Sanmi Koyejo. Investigating data contamination for pre-training language models. arXiv preprint arXiv:2401.06059, 2024.
pairs.why: This is the direct methodological predecessor the paper adopts and extends: training language models from scratch with deliberately inserted contaminated benchmark examples in a controlled setting, which is the experimental basis for the paper's scaling and forgetting conclusions.
pairs.oa_title: Investigating Data Contamination for Pre-training Language Models

pairs.title: Improved Knowledge Distillation via Teacher Assistant
pairs.authors: Seyed Iman Mirzadeh, Mehrdad Farajtabar, Ang Li, Nir Levine, Akihiro Matsukawa, Hassan Ghasemzadeh
pairs.venue: Proc. of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence, vol. 34, pp. 5191-5198
pairs.verbatim: Seyed Iman Mirzadeh, Mehrdad Farajtabar, Ang Li, Nir Levine, Akihiro Matsukawa, and Hassan Ghasemzadeh. Improved knowledge distillation via teacher assistant. In Proc. of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence, volume 34, pp. 5191–5198, 2020.
pairs.why: Introduces an intermediate 'teacher assistant' model to bridge a too-large teacher-student gap, the same core idea GPD's dynamic-teacher mechanism explicitly positions itself against ('existing methods... introducing intermediate-sized assistant teachers').
pairs.oa_title: Improved Knowledge Distillation via Teacher Assistant

pairs.title: Densely Guided Knowledge Distillation using Multiple Teacher Assistants
pairs.authors: Wonchul Son, Jaemin Na, Junyong Choi, Wonjun Hwang
pairs.venue: Proc. of the IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)
pairs.verbatim: Wonchul Son, Jaemin Na, Junyong Choi, and Wonjun Hwang. Densely guided knowledge distillation using multiple teacher assistants. InProc. of the IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision, 2021.
pairs.why: Uses a sequence of intermediate teacher-assistant models with progressively decreasing capacity to control the teacher-student performance gap during distillation, directly overlapping GPD's gap-preserving mechanism.
pairs.oa_title: Densely Guided Knowledge Distillation using Multiple Teacher Assistants

pairs.title: DynamicKD: An Effective Knowledge Distillation via Dynamic Entropy Correction-based Distillation for Gap Optimizing
pairs.authors: Songling Zhu, Ronghua Shang, Bo Yuan, Weitong Zhang, Wenjie Li, Yangyang Li, Licheng Jiao
pairs.verbatim: Songling Zhu, Ronghua Shang, Bo Yuan, Weitong Zhang, Wenjie Li, Yangyang Li, and Licheng Jiao. Dynamickd: An effective knowledge distillation via dynamic entropy correction-based distillation for gap optimizing. Pattern Recognition, 153:110545, 2024a.
pairs.why: Also frames the problem explicitly as 'gap optimizing' via a dynamic distillation correction mechanism, the closest name/purpose match in the paper's own reference list, though the exact publication month relative to the 2024-09-15 cutoff could not be confirmed from the text.
pairs.oa_title: DynamicKD: An effective knowledge distillation via dynamic entropy correction-based distillation for gap optimizing

pairs.title: Dataset Distillation by Matching Training Trajectories
pairs.authors: George Cazenavette, Tongzhou Wang, Antonio Torralba, Alexei A Efros, Jun-Yan Zhu
pairs.venue: Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR), pp. 4750-4759
pairs.verbatim: George Cazenavette, Tongzhou Wang, Antonio Torralba, Alexei A Efros, and Jun-Yan Zhu. Dataset distillation by matching training trajectories. In Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition, pp. 4750–4759, 2022.
pairs.why: Introduces Matching Training Trajectories (MTT), the trajectory-matching mechanism that MKDT directly builds on and adapts (replacing SSL expert trajectories with lower-variance KD-trained student trajectories).
pairs.oa_title: Dataset Distillation by Matching Training Trajectories

pairs.title: Learning Metrics from Teachers: Compact Networks for Image Embedding
pairs.authors: Lu Yu, Vacit Oguz Yazici, Xialei Liu, Joost van de Weijer, Yongmei Cheng, Arnau Ramisa
pairs.verbatim: Lu Yu, Vacit Oguz Yazici, Xialei Liu, Joost van de Weijer, Yongmei Cheng, and Arnau Ramisa. Learning metrics from teachers: Compact networks for image embedding, 2019.
pairs.why: Introduced the specific KD mechanism MKDT reuses -- minimizing MSE between student and teacher representations -- which the paper cites directly as the source of its LKD objective (Eq. 5).
pairs.oa_title: Learning Metrics From Teachers: Compact Networks for Image Embedding

pairs.title: Self-supervised Dataset Distillation for Transfer Learning
pairs.authors: Dong Bok Lee, Seanie Lee, Joonho Ko, Kenji Kawaguchi, Juho Lee, Sung Ju Hwang
pairs.verbatim: Dong Bok Lee, Seanie Lee, Joonho Ko, Kenji Kawaguchi, Juho Lee, and Sung Ju Hwang. Self-supervised dataset distillation for transfer learning, 2023.
pairs.why: KRR-ST is the only prior dataset-distillation-for-SSL method (same domain/purpose), applying kernel-based meta-model matching instead of KD+trajectory matching; it is the paper's main baseline throughout.
pairs.oa_title: Self-Supervised Dataset Distillation for Transfer Learning

pairs.title: AVID: Any-Length Video Inpainting with Diffusion Model
pairs.authors: Zhixing Zhang, Bichen Wu, Xiaoyan Wang, Yaqiao Luo, Luxin Zhang, Yinan Zhao, Peter Vajda, Dimitris Metaxas, Licheng Yu
pairs.verbatim: Zhixing Zhang, Bichen Wu, Xiaoyan Wang, Yaqiao Luo, Luxin Zhang, Yinan Zhao, Peter Vajda, Dimitris Metaxas, and Licheng Yu. Avid: Any-length video inpainting with diffusion model. arXiv preprint arXiv:2312.03816, 2023b.
pairs.why: Directly addresses generative/diffusion-based video inpainting and is cited by the paper as producing 'impressive results,' making it the closest same-domain purpose precedent, though the paper notes it requires user intervention.
pairs.oa_title: AVID: Any-Length Video Inpainting with Diffusion Model

pairs.title: Palette: Image-to-Image Diffusion Models
pairs.authors: Chitwan Saharia, William Chan, Huiwen Chang, Chris A. Lee, Jonathan Ho, Tim Salimans, David J. Fleet, Mohammad Norouzi
pairs.verbatim: Chitwan Saharia, William Chan, Huiwen Chang, Chris A. Lee, Jonathan Ho, Tim Salimans, David J. Fleet, and Mohammad Norouzi. Palette: Image-to-image diffusion models. In SIGGRAPH, pp. 15:1–15:10, 2022.
pairs.why: Establishes that a conditional diffusion model trained to optimality enables exact conditional sampling and semantically consistent generative completion for (image) inpainting -- the same 'generative approach yields semantically consistent completions' purpose this paper extends to video, as the paper itself states it extends this approach.
pairs.oa_title: Palette: Image-to-Image Diffusion Models

pairs.title: Flow-guided Diffusion for Video Inpainting
pairs.authors: Bohai Gu, Yongsheng Yu, Heng Fan, Libo Zhang
pairs.verbatim: Bohai Gu, Yongsheng Yu, Heng Fan, and Libo Zhang. Flow-guided diffusion for video inpainting. arXiv preprint arXiv:2311.15368, 2023.
pairs.why: The closest existing video-diffusion-based inpainting method the paper discusses in related work, though it still follows a content-propagation (optical-flow-guided) approach rather than the pure generative/semantic-consistency purpose claimed here.
pairs.oa_title: Flow-Guided Diffusion for Video Inpainting

pairs.title: Attention Sorting Combats Recency Bias in Long Context Language Models
pairs.authors: Alexander Peysakhovich, Adam Lerer
pairs.verbatim: Alexander Peysakhovich and Adam Lerer. Attention sorting combats recency bias in long context language models. ArXiv, abs/2310.01427, 2023. URL https://api.semanticscholar.org/CorpusID:263609111.
pairs.why: Directly uses LLM attention weights (last generated token) instead of generation as a signal for reordering/using documents; the paper's own ablation shows that removing ICR's aggregation and calibration components reduces it to exactly this prior method ('equivalent to attention sorting').
pairs.oa_title: Attention Sorting Combats Recency Bias In Long Context Language Models

pairs.title: Distilling Knowledge from Reader to Retriever for Question Answering
pairs.authors: Gautier Izacard, Edouard Grave
pairs.verbatim: Gautier Izacard and Edouard Grave. Distilling knowledge from reader to retriever for question answering. In International Conference on Learning Representations, 2021. URL https://openreview.net/forum?id=NTEz-6wysdb.
pairs.why: Prior work cited in the paper's own related work showing that cross-attention between documents and a reader model already carries useful retrieval-relevance signal (used to train better retrievers), supporting the same underlying claim that attention -- not generation -- carries strong ranking signal.
pairs.oa_title: Distilling Knowledge from Reader to Retriever for Question Answering

pairs.title: FIRST: Faster Improved Listwise Reranking with Single Token Decoding
pairs.authors: Revanth Gangi Reddy, JaeHyeok Doo, Yifei Xu, Md Arafat Sultan, Deevya Swain, Avirup Sil, Heng Ji
pairs.verbatim: Revanth Gangi Reddy, JaeHyeok Doo, Yifei Xu, Md Arafat Sultan, Deevya Swain, Avirup Sil, and Heng Ji. First: Faster improved listwise reranking with single token decoding, 2024. URL https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.15657.
pairs.why: Already demonstrates that avoiding full autoregressive generation (using only first-token output logits) can make LLM re-ranking dramatically more efficient without relying on generated text, overlapping the paper's purpose of showing generation is not necessary for extracting re-ranking signals, though it still requires specialized fine-tuning unlike ICR.
pairs.oa_title: FIRST: Faster Improved Listwise Reranking with Single Token Decoding

pairs.title: RULER: What's the Real Context Size of your Long-Context Language Models?
pairs.authors: Cheng-Ping Hsieh, Simeng Sun, Samuel Kriman, Shantanu Acharya, Dima Rekesh, Fei Jia, Boris Ginsburg
pairs.verbatim: Cheng-Ping Hsieh, Simeng Sun, Samuel Kriman, Shantanu Acharya, Dima Rekesh, Fei Jia, and Boris Ginsburg. Ruler: What's the real context size of your long-context language models? COLM, 2024.
pairs.why: RULER itself is designed to reveal where long-context methods succeed or fail across categorized task types (retrieval, multi-hop, aggregation, QA); this paper reuses RULER's own task-category breakdown to characterize Star Attention's success/failure pattern, the same evaluative purpose applied to a new method.
pairs.oa_title: RULER: What's the Real Context Size of Your Long-Context Language Models?

pairs.title: Efficient Streaming Language Models with Attention Sinks
pairs.authors: Guangxuan Xiao, Yuandong Tian, Beidi Chen, Song Han, Mike Lewis
pairs.verbatim: Guangxuan Xiao, Yuandong Tian, Beidi Chen, Song Han, and Mike Lewis. Efficient streaming language models with attention sinks. ICML, 2024.
pairs.why: Identified and characterized the 'attention sink' phenomenon underlying blockwise/local attention approximations, which this paper directly invokes to explain why Star Attention needs anchor blocks and where the block-sparse approximation breaks down.
pairs.oa_title: Efficient Streaming Language Models with Attention Sinks

pairs.title: Ring Attention with Blockwise Transformers for Near-Infinite Context
pairs.authors: Hao Liu, Matei Zaharia, Pieter Abbeel
pairs.verbatim: Hao Liu, Matei Zaharia, and Pieter Abbeel. Ringattention with blockwise transformers for near-infinite context. ICLR, 2024a.
pairs.why: Ring Attention is the paper's own baseline for the accuracy-speed trade-off characterization (Table 1, Table 2); its blockwise-attention design defines the comparison point against which Star Attention's success/failure regions and trade-off are measured.
pairs.oa_title: Ring Attention with Blockwise Transformers for Near-Infinite Context

pairs.title: Orthogonal Subspace Learning for Language Model Continual Learning (O-LoRA)
pairs.authors: Xiao Wang, Tianze Chen, Qiming Ge, Han Xia, Rong Bao, Rui Zheng, Qi Zhang, Tao Gui, Xuanjing Huang
pairs.verbatim: Xiao Wang, Tianze Chen, Qiming Ge, Han Xia, Rong Bao, Rui Zheng, Qi Zhang, Tao Gui, and Xuanjing Huang. Orthogonal subspace learning for language model continual learning. arXiv preprint arXiv:2310.14152, 2023.
pairs.why: O-LoRA is the explicit prior state-of-the-art baseline that CP-Rank is designed to outperform, and its orthogonal-subspace mechanism is the direct predecessor of CP-Rank's rank-adjustment idea.
pairs.oa_title: Orthogonal Subspace Learning for Language Model Continual Learning

pairs.title: LFPT5: A Unified Framework for Lifelong Few-shot Language Learning based on Prompt Tuning of T5
pairs.authors: Chengwei Qin, Shafiq Joty
pairs.verbatim: Chengwei Qin and Shafiq Joty. Lfpt5: A unified framework for lifelong few-shot language learning based on prompt tuning of t5. arXiv preprint arXiv:2110.07298, 2021.
pairs.why: LFPT5 is the previous best-performing baseline (before O-LoRA) on the same standard CL benchmark and task-order protocol that CP-Rank's superiority claims are benchmarked against.
pairs.oa_title: LFPT5: A Unified Framework for Lifelong Few-shot Language Learning Based on Prompt Tuning of T5

pairs.title: Progressive Prompts: Continual Learning for Language Models
pairs.authors: Anastasia Razdaibiedina, Yuning Mao, Rui Hou, Madian Khabsa, Mike Lewis, Amjad Almahairi
pairs.venue: The Eleventh International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR)
pairs.verbatim: Anastasia Razdaibiedina, Yuning Mao, Rui Hou, Madian Khabsa, Mike Lewis, and Amjad Almahairi. Progressive prompts: Continual learning for language models. In The Eleventh International Conference on Learning Representations, 2023.
pairs.why: ProgPrompt supplies both the 15-dataset large-number-of-tasks benchmark and a strong SOTA baseline against which CP-Rank's superiority claims on that benchmark are measured.
pairs.oa_title: Progressive Prompts: Continual Learning for Language Models

pairs.title: Exploring Scaling Trends in LLM Robustness
pairs.authors: Nikolaus Howe, Michał Zając, Ian McKenzie, Oskar Hollinsworth, Tom Tseng, Pierre-Luc Bacon, Adam Gleave
pairs.verbatim: Nikolaus Howe, Michał Zajac, Ian McKenzie, Oskar Hollinsworth, Tom Tseng, Pierre-Luc Bacon, and Adam Gleave. Exploring scaling trends in llm robustness. arXiv preprint arXiv:2407.18213, 2024.
pairs.why: Directly cited in the introduction as a work arguing scaling improves safety benchmark performance, the exact competing prior claim about model-scale vs. vulnerability that this paper's finding overturns.
pairs.oa_title: Exploring Scaling Trends in LLM Robustness

pairs.title: Safetywashing: Do AI Safety Benchmarks Actually Measure Safety Progress?
pairs.authors: Richard Ren, Steven Basart, Adam Khoja, Alice Gatti, Long Phan, Xuwang Yin, Mantas Mazeika, Alexander Pan, Gabriel Mukobi, Ryan H. Kim, Stephen Fitz, Dan Hendrycks
pairs.verbatim: Richard Ren, Steven Basart, Adam Khoja, Alice Gatti, Long Phan, Xuwang Yin, Mantas Mazeika, Alexander Pan, Gabriel Mukobi, Ryan H. Kim, Stephen Fitz, and Dan Hendrycks. Safetywashing: Do AI Safety Benchmarks Actually Measure Safety Progress? arXiv preprint arXiv:2407.21792, 2024.
pairs.why: Cited alongside Howe et al. as the other work claiming capability scaling correlates with improved safety, framing the exact scaling-vs-vulnerability debate this paper's finding resolves in the opposite direction.
pairs.oa_title: Safetywashing: Do AI Safety Benchmarks Actually Measure Safety Progress?

pairs.title: Jailbroken: How Does LLM Safety Training Fail?
pairs.authors: Alexander Wei, Nika Haghtalab, Jacob Steinhardt
pairs.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 36
pairs.verbatim: Alexander Wei, Nika Haghtalab, and Jacob Steinhardt. Jailbroken: How does llm safety training fail? Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, 36, 2023.
pairs.why: Provides the 'mismatched generalization' hypothesis that this paper explicitly contrasts its own 'computational overload' explanation against, and its capability-parity argument for guardrails is directly tested in the paper's guardrail-defense section.
pairs.oa_title: Jailbroken: How Does LLM Safety Training Fail?

pairs.title: Cognitive Overload: Jailbreaking Large Language Models with Overloaded Logical Thinking
pairs.authors: Nan Xu, Fei Wang, Ben Zhou, Bang Zheng Li, Chaowei Xiao, Muhao Chen
pairs.verbatim: Nan Xu, Fei Wang, Ben Zhou, Bang Zheng Li, Chaowei Xiao, and Muhao Chen. Cognitive overload: Jailbreaking large language models with overloaded logical thinking. arXiv preprint arXiv:2311.09827, 2023.
pairs.why: The paper explicitly acknowledges (Section 6) that Xu et al. (2023) already introduced cognitive-overload-based jailbreaking with three variants, making this near-identical prior art that the paper claims only to extend/generalize.
pairs.oa_title: Cognitive Overload: Jailbreaking Large Language Models with Overloaded Logical Thinking
